fact: The e-Governance Academy reports that the Government of Uganda, through NITA-U with World Bank support, renewed the Government Enterprise Architecture and the e-Government Interoperability Framework, and that the project delivered an enhanced e-GIF for standardised data exchange across government systems; the source gives no event date, so the 2026-05-27 publication date is used.

The e-Governance Academy reports that NITA-U, with World Bank support, launched the renewal of Uganda's Government Enterprise Architecture and Government Interoperability Framework this week with a multi-agency workshop in Kampala.

The source states that eGA and NITA-U developed the country's GEA and e-GIF five years earlier, and that the frameworks were approaching their five-year milestone and due an update; the year is approximate, from 'five years ago' in a 2026 article.

The Ministry of Health guidelines, dated January 2023, state that the Government of Uganda has spelled out the overall vision of how sectors exchange information in the Uganda eGovernment Interoperability Framework; the guidelines themselves are health-sector only; the source gives no adoption date for the e-GIF, so the January 2023 publication date is used.

The held page describes the published Uganda e-GIF issued by MoICT&NG / NITA-U, dated 2021-05-06, setting twelve principles and six interoperability layers for e-government systems; it does not itself state an adoption act, and the date is the publication date.
